findings.message: `clutch.help` passes `snap.helpPick` straight to `showQuickPick`. The snapshot marks separators as `{"kind": "separator", "label"}` (clutch/help.py:234), but VS Code only treats an item as a separator when `kind === vscode.QuickPickItemKind.Separator` (-1). So every topic kind ('view', 'command', 'verb', 'section', ...) shows up as an ordinary item the user can select. Selecting one has no `command` and no `topic`, so nothing happens.
findings.paved_road: When building the QuickPick list, map the closed snapshot value through a lookup table, e.g. `const KIND = { separator: vscode.QuickPickItemKind.Separator }` and `items.map(i => i.kind ? { ...i, kind: KIND[i.kind] } : i)`. Add `QuickPickItemKind` to a test mock only if a harness calls it.

findings.message:
The Recent Steps tooltip passes `step.tooltip` (`date · stem · text
what
Before: ...
After: ...`) as raw Markdown into a `MarkdownString`. Markdown treats a single `
` as a soft break, so the what/Before/After lines render as one run-on paragraph. Markdown characters in the step text, such as `_` in outcomes like `needs_human`, are also interpreted, and they are interpreted inside a string marked `isTrusted = true`.
findings.paved_road: Build it as `new vscode.MarkdownString().appendText(step.tooltip).appendMarkdown(`\n\n[Learn more](command:clutch.openHelp?...)`)`. `appendText` escapes the text and keeps its line breaks. Limit trust with `isTrusted = { enabledCommands: ['clutch.openHelp'] }`. Add the `appendText`/`appendMarkdown` members to the `MarkdownString` mock in tests/vscode_step_icons.js.

findings.message: The lock and commit-lock titles used to show `snap.lock` / `snap.commitLock`, the lock holder. That was the only place the header showed who holds each lock. The diff replaces it with the help topic text, so hovering a 🔒 no longer tells the operator which process holds it. The ticket asks to add help to the lock icons, not to remove the holder information (same regression for `commitLock.title` at line 49).
findings.paved_road: Keep the holder and add the help, e.g. `lock.title = [snap.lock || 'unlocked', snap.help[snap.headerHelp.engine].text].join('\n')`, and do the same for `commitLock`.
